subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the existing Gateway HTTP, SDK/RPC, and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required for each?
rationale: The remaining request can expose privileged filesystem, process, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Land narrow gated slices
options.body: Keep this umbrella open and review the active host-FS/readiness PRs only if they preserve safe defaults, owner gates, audit coverage, docs, compatibility proof, and real behavior proof.

options.title: Stop at shipped surfaces
options.body: Declare the existing Gateway HTTP, SDK/RPC, and command-cron paths sufficient and reject host-FS, exec, slash, and CLI direct dispatch until a new maintainer-sponsored design exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow wider direct tool dispatch only with a named security design, explicit operator controls, upgrade proof, and a clear removal path for unsafe defaults.

recommendation.title: Land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Keep this umbrella open and review the active host-FS/readiness PRs only if they preserve safe defaults, owner gates, audit coverage, docs, compatibility proof, and real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is primarily the dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundary, where this history points most strongly to Peter Steinberger.
